article_title: Four Cases on Developer Code: GitHub Published a Training Policy, Anthropic a Retention Policy, and Researchers Reported Grok Build and ZCode Uploads

content_preview.title: Four Cases on Developer Code: GitHub Published a Training Policy, Anthropic a Retention Policy, and Researchers Reported Grok Build and ZCode Uploads
content_preview.summary: GitHub announced a Copilot training opt-out and published Claude Fable retention terms; researchers reported Grok Build and ZCode uploading repositories. The Herald compares where each control sat and how the fixes were checked.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Developers using AI coding tools learned what happens to their code and prompts in two different ways during 2026. [GitHub announced on March 25](https://github.blog/news-insights/company-news/updates-to-github-copilot-interaction-data-usage-policy/) that from April 24 it would use interaction data from Copilot Free, Pro and Pro+ to train its models unless users opt out, and [GitHub's changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-09-01-claude-fable-5-1-generally-available-in-github-...

editor_notes.content_quality: Analysis of 1,685 words (range 800-2000) that examines a topic rather than recapping a release: it compares four cases of developer-code data handling (GitHub's Copilot training opt-out, the Claude Fable retention terms in Copilot, Grok Build uploads, ZCode uploads) and states a thesis explicitly labelled as the Herald's own reading ('no cited source states it in this form'). The four cases are declared as the writer's own selection, not a complete list. Facts and analysis are separated (Background and Current situation are sourced reporting; Comparison is labelled 'the Herald's own tabulation'; Implications are labelled 'follow from the cited reports and are not predictions'). 'What the sources do not settle' reports the July 12 vs 'Monday' disagreement and the unanswered ZCode questions without reconciling them.
editor_notes.source_verification: Integrity: submission v3, hash and Ed25519 signature valid, 11 sources, all HTTPS and allowlisted (github.blog, theregister.com, anthropic.com, techcrunch.com, thenextweb.com, theverge.com, sdxcentral.com, infoworld.com); no allowlist additions. Snapshots source-0..10.html.gz in sources/2026-11/four-cases-on-developer-code-github-published-a-training-policy-anthropic-a-retention-policy-and-researchers-reported-grok-build-and-zcode-uploads/ were all status 200 with real article content (no bot-check pages, no archive fallback); I re-hashed every decompressed snapshot and all 11 sha256 values match the manifest. suspicious_patterns is null for all 11 sources, so no prompt-injection flag arose. I read all 11 from the saved snapshots, as the command prescribes, and did not re-fetch live. source-0 (GitHub blog, Mar 25, 2026): confirms the April 24 date, the Free/Pro/Pro+ scope, 'Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise users are not affected', the 'at rest' exclusion text, 'could be used for model training unless you opt out', and that the data 'will not be shared with third-party AI model providers' (the post also says it may be shared with affiliates including Microsoft, which the article omits). source-1 (The Register, Mar 26 00:13 UTC): confirms /settings/copilot/features, 'thanks to the terms of their contracts', Business/Enterprise exempt (it also says students and teachers are spared; not used). source-2 (GitHub changelog, Sept 1): confirms 'requires data retention by default to operate Anthropic's safety classifiers', 'Retained data is not used to train Anthropic's models', policy off by default for Business/Enterprise, 'Leaving it off keeps Claude Fable 5.1 unavailable', 'through the end of the calendar year', contact the GitHub account team, 'continued use of the models will require EFS', and availability to Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise. source-3 (GitHub changelog, Nov 9): same retention paragraph and end-of-year exemption, now naming Fable 5.2, 5.1 and 5. source-4 (Anthropic, Sep 1): confirms 'introduced 30-day data retention starting with Fable 5', 'not motivated by a desire to train on enterprise data', 'never trained on enterprise data without explicit permission', EFS stores data 'in cloud infrastructure controlled by the customer, not Anthropic', 'starting later this fall', ZDR for eligible customers on Fable 5 and 5.1 'until EFS is ready' (Anthropic gives no calendar date; the end-of-year date is GitHub's, and the article attributes it to GitHub); the post also says customer-owned storage, customer-managed keys and automated review are each opt-in. source-5 (TechCrunch, Sep 1; 'On Tuesday' is correct for Sep 1, 2026): the quoted sentence on monitoring is verbatim; the piece is largely a restatement of Anthropic's announcement (it quotes the announcement's 'never trained' line) and the article does not describe it that way (see corrections). source-6 (The Next Web, Jul 14 20:48 UTC): 'July 12', cereblab, v0.2.93, Google Cloud Storage bucket, the 'nothing from your codebase transmitted to xAI servers during a session' marketing claim, 'did nothing, according to multiple reports', 'no independent audit has confirmed the deletion'. source-7 (The Verge, Jul 14 19:25 UTC, Stevie Bonifield): 'Monday' (= Jul 13; Jul 14, 2026 was a Tuesday), relays The Register, 'files it was told not to open and secrets deleted from history', 'completely and utterly deleted', 'privacy settings are always respected' (in 'a separate post'; the Verge does not name the venue of that second post, the article says 'a post on X'; minor), 'helpful for debugging issues', Cereblab's '/privacy ... per-session retention toggle, not the switch that fixed this', disable_codebase_upload: true, 'no longer fires'. source-8 (SDxCentral, Jul 17): 'found to be active by default', SpaceXAI's later post that retention is switched off by default and retained data deleted (the article words this as SDxCentral having 'wrote that retention was switched off by default'; the source attributes it to SpaceXAI's post), bug bounty $100-$20,000; it calls Cereblab an 'independent AI safety checker'. source-9 (The Next Web, Sep 22 17:10 UTC): ferstar, Sept 18 analysis, 42,411 files, 86.6% Git directories, 564 failed upload attempts (the archive itself 'never made it off his machine'; one smaller 538-file snapshot did reach the server), two settings that 'governed what happened to the data downstream', 'said nothing about automatic workspace snapshots carrying full Git history', Z.ai's post on 'Monday' (= Sep 21), v3.14.0, ferstar's recheck on 21 September, 'The development history is gone, and so is the code that did the uploading', 'rests on the word of the party who deleted', 'Nobody has said how long ZCode behaved this way ... how many workspaces it captured'. source-10 (InfoWorld, Sep 22): 'without their consent', Alibaba Cloud in China, Z.ai asked CAICT and NSFOCUS to assess, 'has never been used for model training', Cris Thomas (Semgrep) quote verbatim; it calls ferstar 'an independent Chinese blogger'. Quote test: all 34 quoted strings in the body (script run over the 11 snapshots, curly quotes and dashes normalised) are present verbatim in a cited snapshot; the one non-quoted literal `disable_codebase_upload: true` is also in the Verge snapshot. Researchers: cereblab and ferstar are named as the outlets name them; the Herald did not read their original posts and the article does not say so (see corrections). Derived figures recomputed: March 25 to April 24 = 30 days (labelled 'By the Herald's count'); November 9 to December 31 = 21 + 31 = 52 days (labelled as conditional on reading 'end of the calendar year' as December 31, 2026, and as the Herald's reading). Weekday checks: Sep 1 Tuesday, Jul 13 Monday, Sep 21 Monday, all consistent with the sources. Absence claims ('none of the GitHub changelogs, Anthropic's post or TechCrunch gives a specific day for EFS availability'; 'No source cited here gives a day for EFS availability') hold against all snapshots (Anthropic says 'later this fall', GitHub 'end of the calendar year' for the ZDR exemption). Outcome claim 'outside retests reported that both uploads had stopped; deletion rests on the vendors' statements or on assessors the vendor engaged' is supported (Verge/TNW for Grok Build, TNW for ZCode; CAICT/NSFOCUS were engaged by Z.ai per InfoWorld and TNW). Internal links: /article/2026-03/29-github-will-train-ai-models-on-copilot-user-interactions-by-default-starting-april-24-sparking-developer-backlash and /article/2026-09/03-claude-fable-51-reaches-github-copilot-on-day-one-requiring-data-retention-by-default both exist and have no corrections record. Analysis independence: at the article level it is met. Counted per outlet: The Register, The Verge, SDxCentral, The Next Web (two articles, one outlet), InfoWorld = 5 independent news outlets, plus TechCrunch (6th, largely restates Anthropic's announcement, counts but should be described as such); GitHub (blog, 2 changelogs) and Anthropic are vendor pages and not counted; the researchers' own posts were not cited. Per case: GitHub training has one independent outlet (The Register); Fable retention has only TechCrunch, a restatement; Grok Build has three (Verge, which relays The Register, SDxCentral, TNW); ZCode has two (TNW, InfoWorld). Anthropic disclosure: required - Anthropic's Fable retention terms are one of the four cases and Anthropic is named in the headline; the one-sentence disclosure ('The Herald's contributor model is built by Anthropic, whose Fable retention terms are one of the four cases.') is present at the end of the Overview, neutral, and does not characterise Anthropic beyond the sources. Anthropic statements in the body are attributive throughout ('says', 'states', 'GitHub's changelog says'); xAI/SpaceXAI and Z.ai statements are attributed to the outlets reporting them and no wrongdoing is asserted beyond what they report. Claim-accuracy greps (quantifier/absence terms) were run and each hit tested against all snapshots; 'both uploads stopped', 'in both discovered cases' and 'the two announced cases' hold for every case.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No wrong statement in the headline, summary or lead. GitHub is correctly named as the publisher of the training policy and the Copilot Fable terms; Anthropic's own post is cited for the 30-day retention and EFS; each date is attributed to the page that gives it (April 24 and March 25 to GitHub's post, end of calendar year to GitHub's changelogs, 'later this fall' to Anthropic). The Grok Build date disagreement (TNW July 12 vs the Verge's 'Monday', July 13) is reported side by side without reconciliation. Musk's 'privacy settings are always respected' is exact and attributed to The Verge, with SpaceXAI's /privacy statement and Cereblab's response reported next to it. Three subordinate points need public clarification (see corrections): the article does not say that TechCrunch largely restates Anthropic's announcement, although it is the only non-vendor outlet cited for the Fable retention case; the findings of cereblab and ferstar are known only through press reports (the Herald did not read their posts) and the ZCode snapshot ferstar examined never left his machine, while a smaller one reached the server; and the article's 'describes a replacement, Enterprise Frontier Safeguards' goes beyond the Anthropic post, which presents EFS as a solution with opt-in controls and interim ZDR 'until EFS is ready'. Minor, not filed: the 'in a post on X' venue for the second Musk post is implied, not stated, by The Verge; SDxCentral's 'retention switched off by default' is SpaceXAI's own post as relayed, worded in the article as SDxCentral's report; the article mentions GitHub's 'not shared with third-party AI model providers' without GitHub's affiliate-sharing statement.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and attributive. Vendor claims are labelled as vendor claims, nobody is accused beyond what outlets report, and the Herald's own readings (30-day notice, 52 days, the thesis, the comparison table) are explicitly labelled. No AI self-reference other than the policy-required one-sentence disclosure.
editor_notes.originality: New. The earlier Herald articles on the Copilot training change (2026-03/29) and Fable 5.1 in Copilot (2026-09/03) are linked for continuity; no published article covers the Grok Build or ZCode uploads or compares these cases. No overlap with recent Copilot articles.
concerns: TechCrunch is cited without the policy-required description of an outlet that largely restates an announcement; it is the sole non-vendor outlet for the Fable retention case (filed as a clarification).

The researchers' findings are second-hand through press reports and the article does not say the Herald did not read the original posts; the ZCode snapshot with 564 failed uploads never left ferstar's machine (filed as a clarification).
'Describes a replacement' for EFS characterises Anthropic's post beyond its wording (filed as a clarification).

Case-level independent sourcing is thin for the first two cases (one independent outlet each, one a restatement), although the Analysis independence requirement is met across the article (5 independent outlets).
recommendations: When citing an outlet that mostly restates a vendor announcement, say so in the sentence that cites it.
State once that findings by named researchers are reported from press coverage when their original posts were not read.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: A careful, well-sourced Analysis that meets the Analysis requirements (1,685 words, 11 sources, 5 independent outlets counted per outlet, thesis labelled as the Herald's own, facts separated from analysis) with every quotation verbatim and every derived figure correct and labelled. Three subordinate clarifications are filed; none touches the headline, summary or lead. Verdict: APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS. Featured candidacy: 2 - cross-vendor comparison of what AI coding tools do with developers' code and where the controls sit, relevant to a broad developer audience, though the Fable retention case rests on vendor pages and a single restating outlet
